question: Can the previously successful full fixed-grid Pi0 memory interface learn three swaps when action loss is removed?

controlled_input.current_visual_frame: frame 60 is replaced by frame 59 before encoding to prevent robot-approach target leakage

architecture.spatial_reduction: fixed 2x2 average pooling, 16x16 patches to K=64 tokens per frame
architecture.temporal_model: non-causal factorized temporal/spatial Transformer, width 256, depth 2, 8 heads
architecture.reader: current tokens cross-attend to history memory every 4 SigLIP layers with fixed effective gate 1.0
architecture.readout: attention-pooled classifier over current tokens after memory reads

initialization.temporal_position_extension: copy learned positions 0..29; initialize new positions 30..59 to zero

stage_1_history_readout.description: Train the K64-to-M128 history path and current-token classifier; freeze the pretrained Pi0 memory reader.

stage_2_reader_ce.description: Continue from Stage 1, freeze the history path, and train only the periodic Pi0 memory readers and current-token classifier, matching the successful one-swap reader stage.

reader_diagnostic.interpretation: Reader updates became much larger without improving validation accuracy; reader under-training is not the primary bottleneck.

conclusion.most_likely_bottleneck: The shallow non-causal history encoder learns weak global correlations but not a reusable sequential cup-identity update operation across three swaps.
conclusion.next_control: Attach classification losses after swap 0, swap 1, and swap 2 using one shared classifier, then measure per-swap accuracy. This distinguishes loss of identity at a particular transition from final-memory/readout compression failure.
